messages.author: 701dadf5d5bd3f3b
messages.subject: Re: p value and adjusted p value
parts: Adjusted p-values control for the multiplicity of testing. Since we fit a separate model, and conduct a separate comparison for each protein, the number of tests equals the number of comparisons. A 0.05 cutoff of an adjusted p-value controls the False Discovery Rate in the collection of tests over all the proteins at 5%. Since they account for the multiplicity, adjusted p-values are more conservative (i.e. it is more difficult to detect a change). The p-values are adjusted by the method of Benhamini and Hochberg, and are sometimes referred to as q-values. All this is for the quantitative comparison only, and is completely unrelated to the FDR, q-values etc reported for identification (e.g. with database search in DDA experiments).

messages.author: df9ba0266a9a081f
messages.subject: Re: p value and adjusted p value
parts:
Dear Diego,

'pvalue' column is calculated by Tvalue (test statistics : calculated by log fold change and standard error) and DF(degree of freedom). and adjusted p-value means that the 'pvalue' column are adjusted for comparisons across multiple proteins using the approach by Benjamini and Hochberg. (there is reference in p21 of MSstats.daily 2.1.5 user manual at workflow webpage.)

about zero value in p value : this is not normal. Yes, this is approximation problem. when pvalue is equal to 0, this means really close to 0.

I hope it will be helpful for you.

Meena
